description: Scoring and analysis rules for a Cinch containment assessment. Single source of truth: read by the Python engine (src/cinch/assess.py) and by the dashboard engine (docs-site/index.html). Change a rule here and both follow.

grades.label: Contained
grades.meaning: Controls are enforced across every pillar; residual risk is accepted and evidenced.

grades.label: Largely contained
grades.meaning: No critical exposure; a small number of non-critical gaps remain scheduled.

grades.label: Conditional
grades.meaning: Deployable only with compensating controls and a dated remediation plan.

grades.label: At risk
grades.meaning: A single bad model decision can plausibly reach production systems.

grades.label: Uncontained
grades.meaning: The environment does not constrain the agent; do not run it against production.

grade_caps.reason: an unenforced critical control caps the grade regardless of score
three or more critical gaps means the containment story does not hold

now.goal: Close every critical containment gap before the next production release.
now.exit: 0 critical gaps; each closure has a verification note attached.

next.goal: Remove the high-severity gaps that turn a contained incident into a broad one.
next.exit: 0 high gaps, or an accepted-risk record naming the owner and expiry.

later.goal: Finish the long tail and keep the assessment complete as the deployment changes.
later.exit: Every applicable control is reviewed and re-assessed on each material change.
